title: Underlying abelian cohomology respects a module inverse-image square
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $g:X'\to X$, $i:X_0\to X$, $j:X'_0\to X'$, $k:X'_0\to X_0$ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] with $g\circ j=i\circ k$. For a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and $q\geq0$, write $F_{ab}$ for its underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and $H^q$ for etale cohomology, with pullback maps as in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. There exist additive equivalences $c_1:H^q(X_0,i^{-1}F_{ab})\simeq H^q(X_0,(i^{-1}F)_{ab})$, $c_2:H^q(X',g^{-1}F_{ab})\simeq H^q(X',(g^{-1}F)_{ab})$, and $c_3:H^q(X'_0,j^{-1}(g^{-1}F)_{ab})\simeq H^q(X'_0,k^{-1}(i^{-1}F)_{ab})$ such that for every $x\in H^q(X,F_{ab})$ one has $c_3(j^*(c_2(g^*x)))=k^*(c_1(i^*x))$. No cohomological bijectivity or geometric condition beyond commutativity is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the existing coefficient-forgetting isomorphisms alpha for i and beta for g from lemma-weil-pbc-etale-pullback-forget-modules. No choice of coherence for these isomorphisms is needed for this existential assertion.

Let e1 be the inverse-image composition isomorphism for j,g and e2 that for k,i with common composite j after g. Define gamma as j inverse image of beta, then e1 inverse, then e2, then k inverse image of alpha inverse. Cohomology of alpha inverse, beta inverse, and gamma gives c1,c2,c3. Each is bijective because the cohomology functor sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms.

Naturality of cohomologyMap moves beta inverse and alpha inverse past the respective pullbacks. Apply the composition part of lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial to j,g and k,i, using the supplied equality of composites. Compose cohomology maps and cancel j inverse image of beta inverse with j inverse image of beta, and e1 with e1 inverse. Both sides become cohomology of e2 followed by k inverse image of alpha inverse applied to pullback along the common composite. This is the required equation.
